readme:
# Riemannian geometry: curvature and comparison

This is Part II of Hopf-Rinow. It begins after the shared connection, exponential, normal-neighbourhood and first-variation APIs. The curvature/volume carrier stays with GeometricTopology and the early cut-locus interface with OptimalTransport. The companion reader gives the explicit fixed-frame proofs and the intrinsic/global bridge obligations.

Use smooth finite-dimensional boundaryless manifolds for the geometric stages; assume connectedness, completeness and dimension bounds only where stated. The analytic prefix works on actual curves in a real Hilbert space. The sign convention is J''+R(J,gamma')gamma'=0 and I(V,W)=integral(<V',W'>-<R(V,gamma')gamma',W>), with half-energy but no half in its Hessian. Endpoint and right-minus-left jump terms must be retained. A moving orthonormal frame is not necessarily parallel.

All stages below are required. Each global proof must be decomposed before the design is closed. The current packet provides the fixed-model prefix, not a completed global theory. Synthetic curvature-dimension/transport regularity, Ricci-flow geometrization and new minimal-submanifold theories are outside these stated endpoints.

The source spine is Ballmann's 2015 energy notes, 2016 Riccati/volume notes and 2003 global-geometry notes. Source corrections in the packet fix the normal-exponential target and Ricci normalization in the author copies; no unqualified assertion is made about another edition.

## RG.0: Jacobi equations and index forms in a parallel model

Construct Wronskians and the index form on actual functions. Prove the Green, broken-field jump and Riccati factorization identities before their intrinsic application.

## RG.1: Intrinsic Jacobi fields and second variation

Construct the actual parallel-frame comparison, variation/Jacobi correspondence and second variation, importing the connection, first variation and curvature from their owners. Keep conjugate and cut times distinct.

## RG.2: Index lemma and curvature comparison

Build actual invertible Jacobi tensors and Riccati solutions on their natural intervals, then the index lemma, Rauch and distance-Hessian comparison with all singular-endpoint and cut-locus conditions.

## RG.3: Curvature and global topology

Prove Bonnet-Myers with Ric >= (m-1) kappa g and kappa > 0, and Hadamard-Cartan with completeness and simple connectivity stated where needed.

## RG.4: Volume distortion and Bishop-Gromov

Construct the polar Jacobian and its integration up to cut time, prove volume-ratio monotonicity in the model-radius range, and separate rigidity from the inequality.

## RG.5: Morse index and closed geodesics

Count interior conjugate multiplicities as index and endpoint multiplicity as nullity. Build the actual broken-geodesic approximation and minimax argument for a nonconstant closed geodesic on a compact positive-dimensional manifold, retaining the free-loop velocity condition.

The exact stage descriptions below and the companion reader supply the complete targets and remaining source work. None is an implementation claim.

stages.title: Jacobi equations and index forms in a parallel model
stages.description: Develop Wronskians, the symmetric index form, endpoint and broken-field Green identities on actual Hilbert-space-valued curves. Prove two-zero uniqueness for nonpositive symmetric curvature coefficients and the square-completion identity for an actual symmetric Riccati solution. Regularity is neighbourhood regularity at each point of the closed interval, not a derivative of arbitrary off-interval extensions. The manifold interpretation requires a constructed orthonormal parallel frame and is not baked into these definitions.

stages.title: Intrinsic Jacobi fields and second variation
stages.description: Import the actual Levi-Civita connection, along-curve derivative and geodesics from HopfRinow, and curvature from GeometricTopology. Prove the parallel-frame comparison: ordinary derivatives of model fields represent covariant derivatives, and K(t)=R(-,gamma')gamma' is the actual symmetric operator. Reuse the owned first-variation and half-energy definitions; construct the two-parameter second-variation formula, all endpoint acceleration terms and the fixed-endpoint specialization. Construct Jacobi fields by the actual variation/ODE correspondence and identify the kernel of d exp with Jacobi fields vanishing at the two specified times. Keep full and normal Jacobi fields distinct. General piecewise fields and partition-independence of their index form require their actual carrier and gluing proof; a single globally differentiated nonsmooth function is not a substitute. Conjugate times are not identified with cut times.

stages.title: Index lemma and curvature comparison
stages.description: Construct Jacobi tensors and their invertibility interval; define S=Y'Y inverse there and prove symmetry from the Wronskian condition. Do not assume a global Riccati solution or cross its poles. Prove the index lemma for fixed endpoint fields when there are no conjugate times in (a,b], and the corresponding equality characterization. Establish scalar and matrix Riccati comparisons with explicit initial or singular-endpoint asymptotics. Derive Rauch comparison for normal Jacobi fields with matching initial norms and appropriate ordered sectional-curvature bounds, restricting to the comparison interval before the relevant first conjugate time. Build the constant-curvature sin/t/sinh model solutions with their actual normalization, and derive distance-Hessian comparison only on the smooth distance locus away from the basepoint and cut locus. The common cut-locus API remains with OptimalTransport; its early geometric supplier must not depend on this volume-comparison output.

stages.title: Curvature and global topology
stages.description: For a complete connected boundaryless smooth Riemannian m-manifold, m>=2, prove Bonnet-Myers under Ric(v,v)>=(m-1) kappa ||v||^2 with a fixed kappa>0, giving diameter at most pi/sqrt(kappa). Use Hopf-Rinow to obtain compactness, and lift the metric to the genuine universal cover to prove that the fundamental group is finite. Pointwise positive Ricci without a uniform lower bound is not this hypothesis. Under sectional curvature <=0, prove absence of conjugate points from the intrinsic Jacobi comparison, completeness of the pulled-back exponential metric, and that exp_p is a universal covering. With simple connectivity of M it is a global diffeomorphism, and geodesic uniqueness/minimization follows with the correct parameterization. Without simple connectivity do not claim injectivity; a flat torus is a required test. No metric completeness statement is deduced from the coordinate ODE alone.

stages.title: Volume distortion and Bishop-Gromov
stages.description: Use the existing Riemannian volume measure and the owned cut-locus measurability/volume-nullity, with the actual exponential polar Jacobian. For m>=2 and Ric>=(m-1) kappa g, derive the trace Riccati inequality and the Jacobi determinant estimate with its t^(m-1) asymptotic. Integrate only up to the cut time, extending the radial density by zero after it; do not integrate a signed Jacobi determinant beyond its first conjugate time. Prove that Vol(B_p(r))/v_(kappa,m)(r) is nonincreasing and at most one for positive ordered radii, with the model radius below pi/sqrt(kappa) when kappa>0. Here v is the actual constant-curvature ball volume in the stated range. Separate the local Euclidean asymptotic, monotonicity, and equality/rigidity proofs. The point-polar change-of-variables formula and finite volume of bounded balls must be proved under the complete finite-dimensional hypotheses. Synthetic CD/RCD and transport regularity remain with their existing owners.

stages.title: Morse index and closed geodesics
stages.description: Prove the Morse index theorem for fixed-endpoint geodesics: index is the sum of conjugate multiplicities at interior times, while nullity is the multiplicity at the final endpoint. Establish finiteness, the actual piecewise-Jacobi finite-dimensional reduction, its orthogonal complement and the change of index through a conjugate time. Do not count endpoint nullity as a negative direction. Construct compact-sublevel finite-dimensional broken-geodesic approximations for the half-energy using the owned normal-neighbourhood and minimizing-geodesic APIs. Prove the required deformation and minimax arguments, and the Birkhoff-Lusternik-Fet existence of a nonconstant closed geodesic on a compact connected boundaryless smooth manifold of positive dimension. A loop critical only among fixed-basepoint paths need not satisfy the periodic-velocity condition: include the free-loop endpoint equations. The point manifold is excluded, and the circle is an acceptance example. Generic homotopy and compactness infrastructure is imported rather than encoded as assumed minimax data.
